newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles schools see revenue growth - paper.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles schools see revenue growth - paper.

text.p: The Los Angeles school district expects its general fund revenues to increase to $4.0 billion in 1999-2000 from $3.8 billion in 1997-1998, according to a published report on Tuesday.
During the same period, however, the district's costs are expected to rise at an even faster pace due to unprecedented enrollment growth, the Los Angeles Times reported.
Superintendent Sid Thompson described the forecast for the nation's second-largest school district as cautiously optimistic, and he urged fiscal prudence, the Times reported.
A $2.4 billion school construction bond for the district will appear on the April ballot. The bond failed in November.
